# UX/UI Audit Methodology v3 — Reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/render_methodology_doc.py from shared/config/audit_methodology_v3.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Design and rationale: [methodology v3 spec](superpowers/specs/2026-10-05-ux-audit-methodology-v3-design.md).

## Severity

| Level | Penalty | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | 25 | Blocks a key task or excludes a user group; no workaround |
| High | 12 | Seriously hampers a key task; workaround exists |
| Medium | 5 | Friction or confusion; task still completes |
| Low | 1 | Cosmetic / polish |

A finding on a declared key-task path is escalated one level (ceiling: Critical).

## Maturity levels

| Level | Label | Minimum score | Cap rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | Excellent | 90 | Requires no High or Critical |
| 4 | Good | 75 | Requires no Critical |
| 3 | Fair | 55 | — |
| 2 | Weak | 35 | Any Critical caps the axis here |
| 1 | Critical | 0 | — |

AI-assessed findings count toward a score only at confidence ≥ 0.8 with cited elements or a screenshot region.

## Product-type weights

Axes not listed weigh 1.0. An unknown or missing product type uses equal weights.

| Product type | Weights |
|---|---|
| ecommerce | trust 1.5, usability 1.3, performance 1.2 |
| saas | usability 1.5, navigation 1.2 |
| content | content 1.5, navigation 1.3 |
| leadgen | content 1.3, trust 1.3, usability 1.2 |
| finance | trust 1.6, accessibility 1.2 |
| public_service | accessibility 1.6, content 1.3 |

## 1. Usability & Task Flow (`usability`)

**Core question:** Can users complete their key tasks efficiently, with clear feedback and easy recovery from errors?

| Criterion | Title | Weight | Standards | Targets | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `usability.primary_action_clear` | The next step of the key task is obvious | core | NNG:H6, BAYMARD:cta | website, webapp, figma, mobile | ai_assessed |
| `usability.action_feedback` | Every action gives visible feedback | core | NNG:H1 | website, webapp, mobile | measured |
| `usability.loading_state_feedback` | Waits longer than one second show progress | supporting | NNG:H1 | website, webapp, mobile | measured |
| `usability.form_requirements_upfront` | Form requirements are stated before input | core | WCAG22:3.3.2, NNG:H5 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `usability.form_input_effort` | Forms ask only for what is needed, with input help | supporting | BAYMARD:form-fields, WCAG22:1.3.5 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `usability.inline_validation` | Fields are validated as users leave them | supporting | NNG:H9 | website, webapp, mobile | measured |
| `usability.error_recovery` | Failed submits keep input and point to the fix | core | NNG:H9, WCAG22:3.3.3 | website, webapp, mobile | measured |
| `usability.destructive_action_safeguard` | Destructive and binding actions can be confirmed or undone | supporting | NNG:H5, WCAG22:3.3.4 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | manual_only |
| `usability.user_control_exit_undo` | Users can exit, go back, and dismiss | supporting | NNG:H3 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | ai_assessed |
| `usability.task_completion_confirmation` | Task completion is confirmed with next steps | core | NNG:H1 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | manual_only |

## 2. Information Architecture & Navigation (`navigation`)

**Core question:** Can users find what they need and always know where they are and how to get back?

| Criterion | Title | Weight | Standards | Targets | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `navigation.global_nav_present` | A global navigation is present | core | NNG:H6 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `navigation.current_location_indicated` | Current location is indicated | core | NNG:H1, WCAG22:2.4.8 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `navigation.nav_label_scent` | Menu labels predict their content | supporting | NNG:information-scent | website, webapp, figma, mobile | ai_assessed |
| `navigation.nav_structure_depth` | Navigation is shallow and focused | supporting | NNG:H8 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `navigation.consistent_navigation` | Navigation stays consistent across pages | core | WCAG22:3.2.3, NNG:H4 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `navigation.search_where_expected` | Search is available where users expect it | supporting | BAYMARD:search | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `navigation.breadcrumbs_deep_hierarchy` | Deep pages show a breadcrumb | supporting | NNG:breadcrumbs | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `navigation.no_dead_ends` | No dead ends or broken links | core | NNG:H3 | website, webapp, mobile | measured |
| `navigation.logo_links_home` | The logo links to the home page | supporting | NNG:H4 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |

## 3. Visual Design & Hierarchy (`visual`)

**Core question:** Does the visual design make priorities obvious and stay consistent across the interface?

| Criterion | Title | Weight | Standards | Targets | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `visual.visual_hierarchy` | Visual hierarchy matches content priority | core | GESTALT:figure_ground, NNG:H8 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | ai_assessed |
| `visual.gestalt_grouping` | Related items are visually grouped | core | GESTALT:proximity | website, webapp, figma, mobile | ai_assessed |
| `visual.typographic_scale` | Typography follows a clear scale | supporting | ISO9241:125 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `visual.readable_line_length` | Body text lines are a readable length | supporting | ISO9241:125 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `visual.spacing_rhythm` | Spacing follows a consistent rhythm | supporting | GESTALT:similarity | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `visual.colour_purpose` | Colour carries consistent meaning | supporting | GESTALT:similarity | website, webapp, figma, mobile | ai_assessed |
| `visual.component_consistency` | The same component looks and behaves the same everywhere | core | NNG:H4 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `visual.button_hierarchy` | Buttons show a clear primary/secondary hierarchy | supporting | NNG:H8 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `visual.affordance_clarity` | Interactive elements look interactive | supporting | NNG:affordances | website, webapp, figma, mobile | ai_assessed |
| `visual.purposeful_motion` | Motion is quick, purposeful, and respects reduced motion | supporting | NNG:animation-usability | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |

## 4. Content & Microcopy (`content`)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `content.value_proposition_clear` | The value proposition is clear in seconds | core | NNG:H2 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | ai_assessed |

| `content.descriptive_cta_labels` | Action labels say what happens next | core | NNG:H2 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `content.scannable_structure` | Content is structured for scanning | supporting | NNG:scanning | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `content.consistent_terminology` | Terms are used consistently | supporting | NNG:H4 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `content.helpful_error_wording` | Error messages are human and specific | supporting | NNG:H9 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | ai_assessed |
| `content.instructional_text` | Help is offered where users need it | supporting | NNG:H10 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | ai_assessed |
| `content.reassurance_microcopy` | Microcopy answers doubts at decision points | supporting | BAYMARD:checkout | website, webapp, figma, mobile | ai_assessed |

## 5. Accessibility & Inclusion (`accessibility`)

**Core question:** Can people with disabilities perceive, operate, and understand the interface (WCAG 2.2 AA)?

| Criterion | Title | Weight | Standards | Targets | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `accessibility.text_contrast` | Text meets AA contrast | core | WCAG22:1.4.3 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `accessibility.non_text_contrast` | Controls and icons meet 3:1 contrast | supporting | WCAG22:1.4.11 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `accessibility.text_alternatives` | Images have appropriate text alternatives | core | WCAG22:1.1.1 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `accessibility.keyboard_operable` | Everything works with a keyboard, with no traps | core | WCAG22:2.1.1, WCAG22:2.1.2 | website, webapp, mobile | measured |
| `accessibility.focus_visible` | Keyboard focus is clearly visible | core | WCAG22:2.4.7, WCAG22:2.4.11 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `accessibility.focus_order` | Focus order follows the visual order | supporting | WCAG22:2.4.3 | website, webapp, mobile | measured |
| `accessibility.names_labels` | Controls have accessible names and visible labels | core | WCAG22:1.3.1, WCAG22:4.1.2, WCAG22:3.3.2 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `accessibility.structure_headings_landmarks` | Headings and landmarks expose the structure | supporting | WCAG22:1.3.1, WCAG22:2.4.6 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `accessibility.target_size` | Touch targets are large enough | supporting | WCAG22:2.5.8 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `accessibility.reflow_zoom` | Content reflows and survives 200% zoom | supporting | WCAG22:1.4.10, WCAG22:1.4.4 | website, webapp, mobile | measured |
| `accessibility.link_purpose` | Link text makes sense on its own | supporting | WCAG22:2.4.4 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `accessibility.motion_control` | Moving content can be paused | supporting | WCAG22:2.2.2, WCAG22:2.3.3 | website, webapp, mobile | measured |

## 6. Performance & Responsiveness (`performance`)

**Core question:** Does the interface load and respond fast, and adapt properly to every screen size?

| Criterion | Title | Weight | Standards | Targets | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `performance.lcp` | Main content loads quickly (LCP) | core | CWV:LCP | website, webapp, mobile | measured |
| `performance.inp` | Interactions respond quickly (INP) | core | CWV:INP | website, webapp, mobile | measured |
| `performance.cls` | The layout stays stable while loading (CLS) | core | CWV:CLS | website, webapp, mobile | measured |
| `performance.first_render` | The server responds and first content appears quickly | supporting | CWV:FCP, CWV:TTFB | website, webapp, mobile | measured |
| `performance.asset_weight` | Pages are not overweight | supporting | CWV:LCP | website, webapp, mobile | measured |
| `performance.responsive_no_horizontal_scroll` | No horizontal scrolling on mobile | core | WCAG22:1.4.10 | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `performance.viewport_configured` | The viewport is configured and zoom is allowed | supporting | WCAG22:1.4.4 | website, webapp, mobile | measured |
| `performance.mobile_content_parity` | Mobile users get the same essential content | supporting | NNG:mobile-ux | website, webapp, figma, mobile | ai_assessed |
| `performance.font_loading_stability` | Web fonts load without invisible text or jumps | supporting | CWV:CLS | website, webapp, mobile | measured |

## 7. Trust & Credibility (`trust`)

**Core question:** Does the product earn trust through transparency, honest design, and credible signals?

| Criterion | Title | Weight | Standards | Targets | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trust.company_identity_contact` | Company identity and contact are easy to find | core | STANFORD:verifiable-identity | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |

| `trust.security_signals` | Connections and payment are visibly secure | supporting | STANFORD:security | website, webapp, mobile | measured |

| `trust.no_deceptive_patterns` | No deceptive patterns | core | NNG:deceptive-patterns | website, webapp, figma, mobile | ai_assessed |
| `trust.credible_social_proof` | Social proof is specific and verifiable | supporting | STANFORD:third-party-support | website, webapp, figma, mobile | ai_assessed |
| `trust.policies_accessible` | Legal and policy pages are reachable | supporting | STANFORD:transparency | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `trust.content_freshness` | Content looks current | supporting | STANFORD:updated-content | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
| `trust.professional_polish` | No broken images, placeholders, or obvious errors | supporting | STANFORD:professional-design | website, webapp, figma, mobile | measured |
